The flight of over two million people from Rwanda into neighbouring countries in 1994, after the genocide. Most were Hutu fleeing the Tutsi-led Rwandan Patriotic Front, which took the country in July. They crossed into Zaire, Tanzania, Burundi and Uganda. Around Goma in eastern Zaire, cholera swept the camps in the first weeks and killed thousands.

The camps held more than refugees. Officials of the old government and the Interahamwe militias who had done much of the killing came too. They took control of the aid, carried off public money and vehicles, bought arms and used the camps as bases to raid Rwanda.

The new government, with Paul Kagame as its strongman, saw the camps as a threat. In 1996 Rwanda backed rebels who attacked them, starting the First Congo War. Many refugees were forced home; others fled west into the forest, where many died. The conflict grew into the Second Congo War from 1998.
